routes.label: Prove a lower bound and reach it

question: Soda is sold in packs of \(6,\) \(12\) and \(24\) cans. What is the minimum number of packs needed to buy exactly \(90\) cans of soda?
solution:
Packs of \(12\) and \(24\) cans always give a whole number of dozens. But \(90=7\times12+6\) is not a whole number of dozens, so an exact purchase must include a \(6\)-pack.

With four or fewer packs, one pack must therefore contain \(6\) cans, and each of the other three packs can contain at most \(24\). Such a purchase has at most
\[
6+3\times24=78<90
\]
cans. Thus at least five packs are necessary.

Five packs do work: three \(24\)-packs, one \(12\)-pack, and one \(6\)-pack contain
\[
3\times24+12+6=90
\]
cans. The minimum is \(\boxed{5}\) packs, choice \(\text{B}\).
